What Is The Most Liked Video On TikTok? Here Are The Top 10
TikTok encourages people to download the app before it’s banned
Here is your comprehensive guide to the most liked TikTok videos EVER.
TikTok is becoming more and more saturated with creators and now it's not always enough to have just one viral video, you need THEE viral video. Whether it's starting a new dance challenge, pulling a hilarious prank, or making some sort of wild announcement, everyone wants to make it onto the TikTok's top 10 list.
Now, we know the likes of Addison Rae and Bella Poarch once had the power to rack up millions of TikTok likes in seconds, but there's actually plenty of new creators who have managed to beat their biggest videos.
In February 2024, a video of strawberries covered in chocolate was posted by @pr4yforgabs and it's now on track to challenge Bella Poarch's long-standing record for the most-liked TikTok video of all time...
Who actually holds the coveted title of having the most-liked video of all time? Here's the current top 10.
1) Bella Poarch 'M to the B' – 66.3 million likes
Bella Poarch has officially earned the most likes on a TikTok video with a whopping 65.8 million likes for simply bopping her head to Millie B's 'M to the B'. The video, which was posted in August 2020, made the 2016 track reach a global audience and sparked a host of copycat videos. It's also the fifth most viewed TikTok of all time with over 825 million views.
2) Nick Luciano's 'Sugar Crush' parody video – 53.1 million likes
Nick Luciano made a copy of @kaylavoid's hilarious video and it quickly went viral. The video currently has over 50 million likes and counting!
3) Jamie32bish's dancing to Nelly Furtado's 'Say It Right' - 52.9 million likes
As well as being one of the most viewed TikToks of all time, Jamie32bish's viral Nelly Furtado clip is also one of the most liked. It's been replicated by huge TikTok stars and celebrities all over the world.
4) Franek Bielak's drawing – 51.7 million likes
Franek might have only been 15 years old at the time, but the artist has earned himself a spot on the most-liked TikTok list for his impressive artwork. This particular piece took a whopping 23 hours to complete.
5) Gabs' strawberries covered in chocolate video – 50.6 million likes
6) Leah Halton's 'Praise Jah In The Moonlight' lipsync video – 50.1 million likes
7) Totouchanemu's dancing to The Kid Laroi and Justin Bieber's 'STAY' - 45.2 million likes
This one is also one of the most viewed TikTok videos of all time! However, due to the removal of songs on TikTok, the sound is no longer available.
8) Billie Eilish's first TikTok video – 41 million likes
Billie Eilish had only just joined TikTok at the time but, unsurprisingly, she immediately made it onto the most-liked list. Billie's first video ever, where she tries out the Time Warp Scan filter, has over 40 million likes and ranks among the most viewed TikToks of all time. Her power.
8) S4r4h43's strawberries covered in chocolate video – 39.6 million likes
9) Nyadollie's beauty tutorial video - 38 million likes
10) Khaby Lame's 'How to peel a banana' video – 37.9 million likes

Bella Poarch really knew how to capture lightning in a bottle, didn't she? After her first massive hit, she dropped another clip that absolutely blew up. This second viral moment proved it wasn't a fluke; she had a real knack for creating content that just clicked with millions.

Unique Visuals: Bella has a distinct style, and this video leaned into that, making it stand out.

It was raw, it was engaging, and it showed how a creator could connect with a massive audience through sheer personality and a good idea. It’s a testament to how TikTok can launch creators into superstardom with just a few seconds of video.
The speed at which these videos gain traction is always astonishing. One minute it's a new sound, and the next, millions are engaging with it. It really highlights the power of trends and how quickly they can spread across the platform.
7.@addisonre – mirror transition
Addison Rae really knows how to make a simple mirror work for her. This particular clip became a huge hit because it’s all about that wow moment when you see the transformation. It’s not just a quick glance; it’s a full reveal.
What makes this transition so good? It’s all in the execution. You start with a casual shot, maybe looking a bit undone, and then with a clever move, you’re suddenly looking completely different. It’s that sudden shift that grabs your attention.
Here’s a breakdown of why it worked so well:
The Setup: A seemingly normal moment, setting the stage for the surprise.
The Reveal: A quick, sharp transition that shows a completely new look.
The Confidence: Addison’s expression and pose after the change sell the entire effect.
It’s a great example of how a simple idea, done with flair, can become incredibly popular. The key is the contrast between the before and after, making the viewer do a double-take. It’s the kind of video that makes you want to rewind and watch it again, just to see how they pulled it off.
8.@cznburak – giant cooking video
Nusret Gökçe, better known as @cznburak, has a knack for making food look not just delicious, but also impressively massive. His TikToks often feature him preparing enormous portions of classic dishes, like a kebab the size of a small car or a salad that requires a wheelbarrow. It's the sheer scale of his culinary creations that grabs attention. He doesn't just cook; he orchestrates food symphonies on an epic scale.
His videos are a spectacle, blending humor with a genuine passion for food. You'll see him expertly slicing, dicing, and seasoning ingredients that would normally feed a small army. It’s a visual feast that’s hard to look away from.
Here's a peek at what makes his giant cooking videos so popular:
Unmatched Portions: We're talking about food quantities that defy logic, making everyday meals look like appetizers.
Signature Style: His iconic salt-sprinkling move, often performed with a flourish on these giant dishes, is a must-see.
Global Appeal: Food is universal, and seeing it prepared on such a grand scale transcends language barriers, bringing smiles to millions.
While the exact ingredients and methods for these colossal meals aren't always detailed, the joy and entertainment value are clear. It's a reminder that sometimes, bigger really is better when it comes to viral content.
It’s not just about the size, though. There’s a certain artistry in how he handles these massive ingredients, making the whole process look surprisingly smooth. You can’t help but be a little mesmerized by the spectacle.
9.@khaby.lame – silent reaction
Khaby Lame has a knack for making the simplest things look ridiculously overcomplicated, and then, with just a look, he brings it all back to common sense. His silent reaction videos are pure gold. You know the drill: someone presents a hack or a solution that's just… absurd. Think cutting a cake with a shoe or trying to open a jar with a drill. Khaby just watches, maybe tilts his head a bit, and then, with that signature hand gesture, he shows the actual easy way to do it. It's the universal language of 'why would you even do that?'
His ability to convey so much without saying a word is pretty amazing. It’s not just about pointing out bad life hacks; it’s about the sheer relatability of seeing someone else’s ridiculousness and knowing there’s a simpler path. It’s a whole vibe, really.
